framework.name: Code Quality & Maintainability Evaluation
framework.description: Evaluates structural quality, maintainability, readability, and technical debt across the FGC Upper Room codebase. Targets the Vite/React frontend, Express backend services, shared utilities, and database layer.

rubric.1-2: Critical: Codebase is unmaintainable, high risk of introducing bugs on any change.
rubric.3-4: Poor: Significant structural problems. Major refactoring needed.
rubric.5-6: Fair: Functional but messy. Technical debt accumulating.
rubric.7-8: Good: Well-structured with minor improvements possible.
rubric.9-10: Excellent: Clean, modular, well-documented, easy to onboard new developers.

scoring.overall_calculation: Weighted average of all category scores.

criteria.name: Directory Organization
what_to_check: Clear separation between frontend, bot, attendance service, and shared code
Consistent folder naming conventions across services
Logical grouping: routes, controllers, middleware, models, utils, config
No orphaned files or directories without clear purpose
README exists at project root AND each service root explaining structure
criteria.remediation: Adopt monorepo structure with clear boundaries. Each service should have: src/, config/, tests/, README.md.

criteria.name: File Size & Complexity
what_to_check: No file exceeds 300 lines (flag files > 200 lines)
Functions/methods are under 50 lines each
Cyclomatic complexity per function is reasonable (< 10)
Check the monolithic server.ts (~1200 lines found in previous audit)
known_issues: server.ts was ~1200 lines in original audit — check current line count after 5 phases of changes. May have been partially refactored or grown further.

Multiple data/*.json files still in use (contact-submissions, newsletter-subscribers, admin-users, admin-sessions, admin-audit-log, admin-blog-posts, admin-media, admin-testimonies, rum-events) — assess whether their read/write logic adds to file complexity
criteria.remediation: Split large files by responsibility. Extract route handlers into separate files. Use a router pattern for Express.

criteria.name: Separation of Concerns
what_to_check: Route handlers don't contain business logic AND database queries
Database access is abstracted (repository/service pattern or at least separate query files)
Configuration is centralized, not scattered across files
Middleware is modular and reusable
Frontend components separate UI from data fetching
criteria.remediation: Implement layers: routes -> controllers -> services -> repositories. Each layer has a single concern.

criteria.name: Consistent Naming
what_to_check: Variables and functions use camelCase (JavaScript convention)
React components use PascalCase
File names match their default export
Database columns use snake_case (PostgreSQL convention)
Constants use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
Boolean variables use is/has/should prefix
No single-letter variables except loop counters
criteria.remediation: Document naming conventions in CONTRIBUTING.md. Add ESLint naming-convention rules.

criteria.name: Meaningful Names
what_to_check: Function names describe what they do (sendServiceReminder, not doStuff)
Variable names are descriptive (memberPhoneNumber, not mpn)
No ambiguous abbreviations
Route paths follow REST conventions (/api/v1/members, not /api/getMembers)
criteria.remediation: Rename unclear identifiers. Follow verb-noun pattern for functions. Use REST conventions for API paths.

criteria.name: Duplicate Code Detection
what_to_check: No copy-pasted blocks of logic across files
Database query patterns are not repeated (extract to shared query functions)
Error handling patterns are consistent (not reimplemented per route)
Validation logic is not duplicated between frontend and backend unnecessarily
WhatsApp message formatting is centralized, not scattered
criteria.remediation: Extract shared logic into utility modules. Create shared middleware for common patterns. Use a query builder for repeated DB patterns.

criteria.name: Dead Code Elimination
what_to_check: No unused functions, variables, or imports
No commented-out code blocks left in production files
No unused React components or pages
No unreachable code paths
No unused npm dependencies
criteria.remediation: Run ESLint no-unused-vars. Use depcheck for unused packages. Remove all commented-out code (git history preserves it).

criteria.name: Known Duplication: maskPhone() and Utility Helpers
what_to_check: maskPhone() helper is duplicated in at least 3 files: bot/src/app.js, bot/src/services/opt-out.service.js, bot/src/routes/giving.js
Check for other utility functions copy-pasted across files (date formatting, phone number normalization, error response helpers)
Verify whether a shared utils/ module exists and is actually used consistently
known_issues: maskPhone() was added during Phase 3-4 in multiple files independently — should be extracted to bot/src/utils/format.js or similar
criteria.remediation: Extract maskPhone() and other repeated helpers to a shared utility module (e.g., bot/src/utils/format.js). Import from the single source everywhere.

criteria.name: Consistent Error Handling
what_to_check: All async functions have try-catch or .catch() handlers
Express routes use async error wrapper or express-async-errors
Database errors are caught and handled appropriately
Redis/BullMQ errors are caught (connection failures, queue errors)
Errors are classified (operational vs programmer errors)
criteria.remediation: Create centralized error handling middleware. Use async wrapper: const asyncHandler = fn => (req, res, next) => fn(req, res, next).catch(next). Define custom error classes.

criteria.name: Error Propagation
what_to_check: Errors bubble up with context (not swallowed silently)
catch blocks don't just console.log and continue silently
Failed operations return appropriate HTTP status codes
Error responses follow a consistent format: { error: string, code?: string }
criteria.remediation: Define error response format. Never swallow errors silently. Add context when re-throwing.

criteria.name: Component Design
what_to_check: Components follow single responsibility principle
No god components (doing too many things)
Props are well-defined (PropTypes or TypeScript interfaces)
Proper use of hooks (no rules of hooks violations)
Custom hooks extract reusable logic from components
No business logic in JSX return statements
criteria.remediation: Split large components. Extract logic into custom hooks. Define prop types.

criteria.name: State Management
what_to_check: State is lifted to the appropriate level (not prop-drilled excessively)
No redundant state (derived values should be computed, not stored)
useEffect dependencies are correct (no missing or extra deps)
No state updates in render phase
Global state (if used) is organized by domain
known_issues: Blog/testimonies were originally localStorage — admin data was migrated to server-side JSON files (data/admin-blog-posts.json, data/admin-testimonies.json). Verify React state management properly fetches from API, not localStorage
criteria.remediation: Audit useEffect dependencies. Remove redundant state. Consider React Query/SWR for server state.

criteria.name: Performance Patterns
what_to_check: React.memo used where appropriate for expensive re-renders
useMemo/useCallback used for expensive computations and stable references
No inline object/array creation in JSX props (causes unnecessary re-renders)
Images are lazy-loaded and optimized
Route-based code splitting with React.lazy
criteria.remediation: Profile with React DevTools. Add memo to list items. Implement code splitting for admin pages.

criteria.name: Inline Documentation
what_to_check: Complex business logic has explanatory comments (why, not what)
API endpoint handlers describe expected input/output
Database queries have comments explaining complex joins or conditions
WhatsApp message flow logic is documented
Magic numbers are named constants with comments
criteria.remediation: Add JSDoc comments to all exported functions. Document complex algorithms. Replace magic numbers with named constants.

criteria.name: API Documentation
what_to_check: All API endpoints are documented (path, method, params, body, response)
Error responses are documented
Authentication requirements per endpoint are documented
WhatsApp command format (@email, STOP, etc.) is documented
criteria.remediation: Create API docs (OpenAPI/Swagger or markdown). Document each endpoint with examples.

criteria.name: Test Existence & Coverage
what_to_check: Unit tests exist for critical business logic (scheduling, message formatting, opt-out)
Integration tests exist for API endpoints
Frontend component tests exist for key user flows
Test runner is configured (Jest, Vitest, or similar)
Tests can be run with a single command (npm test)
Evaluate actual code coverage percentage, not just test existence
known_issues: 10 unit tests currently passing, 9 integration tests (1 flaky deadlock on visitor.repository.test.mjs)
E2E, accessibility, performance, security, and load smoke tests exist in CI
Evaluate actual coverage percentage and whether critical paths (auth, giving, attendance check-in) are covered
criteria.remediation: Fix the flaky visitor.repository.test.mjs deadlock. Add coverage reporting (c8 or istanbul). Target 60% coverage on business logic. Add tests for the new giving flow.

criteria.name: Test Quality
what_to_check: Tests are not just snapshot tests — they test behavior
Edge cases are covered (empty inputs, invalid data, concurrent requests)
Tests are independent (no shared mutable state between tests)
Mocks are used appropriately (external APIs, database)
criteria.remediation: Write behavior tests, not implementation tests. Mock external dependencies. Test error paths.

evaluation_instructions.for_claude_code: Read this framework, then systematically evaluate the codebase. Use tools like: find . -name '*.js' -o -name '*.jsx' -o -name '*.ts' | xargs wc -l (for file sizes), grep -r patterns for conventions, and manual review of key files. Score each criterion 1-10 with evidence. Output markdown report to evaluation/results/.
